# zgeqrt3

> Recursively computes a QR factorization of a complex `M`-by-`N` matrix using the compact WY representation of `Q`.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zgeqrt3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgeqrt3';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zgeqrt3( order, M, N, A, LDA, T, LDT ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `M` | `integer` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Rejects `m < N` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>m × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix; on exit contains `R` and `V` |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Column-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, m)`<br>Row-major requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `T` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output upper triangular factor of the block reflector |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Requires `LDT ≥ max(1, N)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge N$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the complex M-by-N matrix A. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal contain the N-by-N upper triangular matrix R; the elements below the diagonal are the columns of V. See below for further details.
- `T`: The N-by-N upper triangular factor of the block reflector. The elements on and above the diagonal contain the block reflector T; the elements below the diagonal are not used. See below for further details.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `M < N`)
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zgeqrt3.ndarray(
    M,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `M` | `integer` | Number of rows of the matrix `A` (`M >= N`)<br>Rejects `m < N` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>m × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output matrix; on exit contains `R` and `V` |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` (in complex elements) |
| `T` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output upper triangular factor of the block reflector |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `T` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `T` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `T` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge N$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the complex M-by-N matrix A. On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal contain the N-by-N upper triangular matrix R; the elements below the diagonal are the columns of V. See below for further details.
- `T`: The N-by-N upper triangular factor of the block reflector. The elements on and above the diagonal contain the block reflector T; the elements below the diagonal are not used. See below for further details.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument is invalid (rejected when `M < N`)
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zgeqrt3()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZGEQRT3`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zgeqrt3.f).
-   Requires `M >= N`.
-   On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of `A` contain the `N`-by-`N` upper triangular matrix `R`; the elements below the diagonal are the columns of `V` defining the elementary reflectors. The implicit `1`s on the diagonal of `V` are not stored.
-   On exit, the elements on and above the diagonal of `T` contain the `N`-by-`N` upper triangular block reflector factor; the elements below the diagonal are not used.
-   The block reflector is `H = I - V * T * V^H` where `V^H` denotes the conjugate transpose of `V`.
-   Based on the algorithm of Elmroth and Gustavson, _IBM J. Res. Develop._ Vol 44 No. 4, July 2000.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zgeqrt3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zgeqrt3';

// 4x2 complex matrix in column-major order; T is N-by-N = 2-by-2.
const A = new Complex128Array( 8 );
const T = new Complex128Array( 4 );

A.set( [ 2.0, 0.1 ], 0 );
A.set( [ 0.7, -0.3 ], 1 );
A.set( [ 0.5, 0.3 ], 2 );
A.set( [ -1.0, 0.4 ], 3 );
A.set( [ 1.5, -0.2 ], 4 );
A.set( [ 3.0, 0.5 ], 5 );
A.set( [ 1.1, -0.4 ], 6 );
A.set( [ 0.4, 0.2 ], 7 );

const info = zgeqrt3( 'column-major', 4, 2, A, 4, T, 2 );
console.log( info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZGEQRT3`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZGEQRT3 recursively computes a QR factorization of a complex M-by-N matrix A, using the compact WY representation of Q.

Based on the algorithm of Elmroth and Gustavson, IBM J. Res. Develop. Vol 44 No. 4 July 2000.

### Further Details

The matrix V stores the elementary reflectors H(i) in the i-th column below the diagonal. For example, if $M=5$ and $N=3$, the matrix V is

$$
V = \begin{pmatrix} 1 &  &  \\ v_{1} & 1 &  \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & 1 \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \\ v_{1} & v_{2} & v_{3} \end{pmatrix}
$$

where the vi's represent the vectors which define H(i), which are returned in the matrix A. The 1's along the diagonal of V are not stored in A. The block reflector H is then given by

$$
H = I - V \, T \, V^H
$$

where $V^H$ is the conjugate transpose of V.

For details of the algorithm, see Elmroth and Gustavson (cited above).

</section>
